title: Choose the visual world for SmartFlow NLEX
question: Two directions for the whole dashboard, each shown on the Overview with the live counts from 3 Oct 22:56. Pick one, re-roll, or take the category standard.

options.label: Shift Log
options.thesis: Every reading is a log entry: when, from what source, and whether it is still current.
options.viewport: Ink rail; the page as a log of entries, each with a time-and-source gutter; the corridor as a mirrored NB/SB diagram at true km; a stale entry highlighted canary with its age.
options.risk: Light-first: the night-shift dark theme has to be designed, not inverted, and the time gutter costs about 110 px of width on every panel.

raised.raise: Forecast is hatched and observed is solid, everywhere a forecast is drawn.
NB and SB are mirrored either side of one median on every view, never stacked in different orders.
Per-exit small multiples share one fixed scale so exits compare honestly.
Flat colour only: no gradients, glows or glass; depth comes from rules and tone.
Times and values sit flush right in tabular figures.

options.label: Guide Sign
options.lineage: DPWH and NLEX guide signs and km posts
options.thesis: The dashboard reads like the road: every location is a km post, every count a sign legend.
options.viewport: Sign-green rail; three state counts as large condensed numerals; the corridor labelled with km-post tablets; dark-first for the control room.
options.risk: The most obvious association for a highway product, and a green shell sits close to the clear-state green, so the state palette has to be tuned.

options.label: Exposure Record
options.thesis: Load drawn as hatch density over an eleven-step tonal ramp.
options.viewport: Translucent sheets of corridor data overlapping on a backlit ramp.
options.case: Operators do not identify with darkroom practice, and sliding sheets would replace standard navigation.
options.risk: Reads as an art piece on a working screen.
options.kept: Hatching as an honest encoding: forecast hatched, observed solid.

options.label: Labanotation Score
options.thesis: Two carriageways as the two halves of a centre staff.
options.viewport: A vertical corridor spine with NB and SB columns, time flowing upward.
options.case: Bilateral NB/SB is clear, but upward time fights every chart convention operators know.
options.kept: Bilateral law: NB and SB mirrored around one median everywhere.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: Each exit as a plate at one fixed scale.
options.viewport: Exit plates in a row on a shared baseline.
options.case: No audience tie, and cream-and-sepia is the wrong light for a control room.

options.label: Cassette J-card
options.thesis: NB and SB as side A and side B.
options.viewport: A folded tracklist of exits with running times.
options.kept: Running values flush right in tabular figures.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.thesis: Pixel display type over fine text.
options.viewport: Huge pixel numerals over dense columns.
options.case: Coarse type hurts legibility at a distance and on a night shift.
options.kept: Real scale contrast: one face across many sizes.

options.label: Guide Map
options.thesis: Areas as flat lobes of colour.
options.case: Playful leisure grammar is wrong for incident response.
options.kept: Flat, unmodulated colour with no gradients or glow.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean ops dashboard executed well: neutral grey, white cards, one blue.
canonCard.viewport: Stat cards over a corridor card, the arrangement every ops product ships.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other dashboards by design.
